ORDINANCE NO. 1 OF 2023
AN ORDINANCE AFFIRMING AND ESTABLISHING THE ORGANIZATION AND
PROCEDURES OF THE CITY COUNCIL; ESTABLISHING COMMITTEES AND
COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS; REPEALING CONFLICTING LEGISLATION;
DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City Council of Cabot, in keeping with its statutory duty under A.C.A. 14-43-
501, has convened to organize its meetings and procedures for the coming year; and

WHEREAS, the City Council desires to maintain an organizational and procedural structure,
including the use of committees as delineated herein, in order to effectively and efficiently serve the

residents of Cabot; and

WHEREAS, as set forth herein, the Cabot City Council hereby affirms and establishes its
organizational structure and procedures for 2023 and henceforth, unless subsequently altered by this body.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: This governing body hereby adopts procedures to organize itself as set forth
in Exhibit “A”, attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference. Committees and
Committee assignments are established as set forth in Exhibit “B”, attached hereto and incorporated
herein by this reference.

SECTION 2: [If any provision of this Ordinance or its attachments, or the application thereof
is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of the Ordinance, and to
this end, the provisions of this Ordinance and its attachments are declared to be severable.

SECTION 3: All prior ordinances, resolutions, code sections, any other legislation, and any
parts thereof in conflict with this legislation are hereby repealed.

SECTION 4: It is essential for the health and safety of the City of Cabot for the City Council
to be properly organized in order to address any serious and pressing concerns that may arise within
the community. In addition, it is important for the City Council to remain in compliance with the

state statute which requires the City Council to “assemble and organize” in January. An emergency

City Council Meeting Organizational Structure

1. Work Session Meetings

Work Session meetings shall customarily be held on the first Monday of every month at
6:30 p.m. The date and time may be changed in the case of scheduling conflicts or as needed.
These Work Session meetings are utilized to allow council members and each standing committee
to discuss details of proposed legislation with City staff in a more informal setting. The Work
Session shall be called to order by the Mayor who will then recognize the chair of each committee
in turn to discuss the items on the agenda relevant to that committee. Each committee chair shall
preside over the discussion of agenda items relevant to his or her committee and may conduct
votes amongst his committee members to forward any piece of proposed legislation on to a regular
council meeting or for any other appropriate purpose. No readings or votes for final passage of
legislation shall be conducted during Work Session meetings.

At the conclusion of each Work Session meeting, a Regular Session Council meeting shall
be held. At this meeting any formal reading, votes for final passage, or other appropriate action
may be taken in regards to any motion or piece of legislation. This meeting need not be conducted
if there are no items on its agenda for consideration.

2. Regular Session Meeting

Regular Session meetings shall customarily be held on the third Monday of each month at
6:30 p.m. The date and time may be changed in the case of scheduling conflicts or as needed. At
these meetings any formal reading, votes for final passage, or other appropriate action may be
taken in regards to any motion or piece of legislation. Pursuant to state law, these meetings shall
be presided over by the Mayor, with each council member having an opportunity to discuss any
item, make any appropriate motion, and vote when appropriate.

Only items on the agenda may be discussed, read, or voted on, unless the agenda is
amended to add that particular item by 2/3 vote of all elected council members. An item not on
the agenda may be discussed, though not voted on, during the community input section of the
meeting.

Pursuant to state law, any motion to suspend the rules, waive readings, approve or attach
an emergency clause, or similar motion must be passed by 2/3 vote of all elected council members

3. Location

The Veterans Park Event Center is the regular meeting place for the Cabot City Council.
The Cabot City Annex or other appropriate location may also be used if needed.

4, Dates of Meetings

Specific dates of meetings shall be set out in other legislation adopted for that purpose.

5. Agendas for Meetings

The agenda for the Work Session meetings shall be coordinated by the Mayor's office.
Any council member may request to have an item added to a Work Session meeting agenda. A
Work Session agenda, along with appropriate documents, should be forwarded to council
members by 4:00 p.m. on the Thursday before the meeting if possible.

The agenda for the Regular Session meetings shall be coordinated by the Mayor's office.
Items may be placed on this agenda by the Mayor, by majority vote of the Council, or by majority
vote of the appropriate committee at a Work Session meeting or other committee meeting. A
Regular Session agenda, along with appropriate documents, should be forwarded to council
members by 4:00 p.m. on the Thursday before the meeting if possible.

In order to be placed on an agenda, a legislative item must be sponsored by either a
council member or the Mayor. Ifa legislative item is forwarded to the Council from one of the
city’s independent commissions it must be sponsored by that independent commission.

Agendas are considered final once forwarded to council members and legislative items
may not be added after that point except upon 2/3 vote of all elected Council members. However,
an item may be added to the agenda after it was sent out but before the start of the meeting upon
joint agreement of the Mayor and the City Council President Pro Tempore.

6. President Pro Tempore

Ed Long, as longest serving member of the Cabot City Council, is hereby named City
Council President Pro Tempore.

7. Mayor and City Council Relationship

In exercising its management responsibilities, the City Council reserves its authority
to approve policy which represents broad statements of its intentions, approves plans and
programs, and delegates authority of administration to the Mayor, except those rights that
are by law conferred upon or reserved to the city council. Pursuant to state law, the City
Council delegates the authority to the Mayor to hire capable personnel within an approved
wage and salary policy, to plan and establish schedules and to train, supervise and terminate
employees. Per A.C.A. § 14-42-110, the City Council reserves the authority to review the
hiring or removal of a department head and may overturn the hiring or removal of a
department head by the Mayor upon two-thirds majority of all elected Council members.

8. Further Responsibilities of the Mayor

The Mayor has the principal responsibility for directing the operations of the city
government and for advising and assisting the City Council in its deliberations. In connection
with the latter responsibility, the City Council requests the Mayor to furnish it with whatever
--- page 10 (OCR) ---
data, information, and material it may need to properly carry out its functions in an informed
manner.

The Mayor also has the principal responsibility to ensure that the city's administrative
officers and department heads understand and obey all local, state, and federal laws
pertaining to the city's operations, and when a violation of any law is discovered, that
appropriate disclosure is made to the City Council and proper and adequate disciplinary
measures are taken against the responsible employee or employees.

9. Further Responsibilities of the Council

It is the responsibility of City Council members to be engaged and present at meetings in
representing the residents of Cabot. If any member of the City Council is absent for either three
consecutive meetings or four total meetings in a calendar year then a Resolution of Reprimand
shall be considered by the Council. Absences may be excused at a council member’s request and
by joint agreement of the Mayor and the President Pro Tempore of the City Council.

It is the further responsibility of council members to hold themselves to a high ethical and
moral standard in representing the residents of Cabot. Any member who fails to live up to these
standards or who brings embarrassment or disrepute to the City Council may also be subject to a
Resolution of Reprimand.

10. City Council and Mayor Cooperation

Efficient management of the city can exist only through mutual understanding and
complete cooperation between the City Council and the Mayor. The Mayor's performance
cannot be of the best unless he is given the latitude to exercise independent judgment in
executing policies of the City Council. The City Council acknowledges that obligation and
gives the Mayor the latitude of judgment and discretion, and expects faithful performance in
carrying out the policies of the City Council.

It shall be understood that administrative authority for the management of the city
rests with the Mayor. Members of the City Council should refrain, as individuals, from giving
specific direction or instruction to city personnel pertaining to the discharge of assigned
duties, however, open communication between aldermen and city employees is encouraged
and expected to guarantee sound decisions based upon the free flow of information.

MEMORANDUM

TO: Cabot City Council

FROM: Little Rock Air Force Base CUSI Project

SUBJECT: Proposed Regional Planning Commission Resolution (RPC) regarding a Little Rock
Air Force Base long-term planning solution

DATE: January 2, 2023

Cities and Counties included in the proposal:

Jacksonville Austin Pulaski County

Cabot Ward Lonoke County

Sherwood Maumelle White County

North Little Rock Faulkner County
Quick History:

To minimize any encroachment on the missions of the LRAFB, a Compatible Use Study for the
Department of Defense has been conducted by a highly qualified consulting firm and
representatives of the jurisdictions listed above. The consulting firm, of White & Smith Planning
and Law Group, has performed many such studies nationwide. This study has been an ongoing
project for over three years with representatives from each of the cities and counties involved
attending numerous planning meetings and providing considerable input on this subject. The
project has been managed by the City of Jacksonville and is designed to maximize the LRAFB
Mission and training environment and enhance community growth in the region. The study and

implementation of the project have cost over $1 million and has been funded by DoD and State
government.

There are two working groups on this project: an Executive Committee and an Implementation
Committee. These Committees have worked with the project planners to develop a
comprehensive set of recommendations to protect the LRAFB from the encroachment of
incompatible land uses and to otherwise secure the Base’s ongoing presence in the region and
full operational capacity.

The 2021 “Compatible Use Study” report recommended the creation of an informal staff-level
“Military Planning and Coordination Committee (MPCC)” created pursuant to a non-binding
“memorandum of understanding” (MOU). The Committees have considered several iterations of
a draft MOU prepared by White and Smith. The MOU represents an informal means of trying to
align the regulatory approach of each of the jurisdictions with respect to limitations on tall

' structures and other uses that could impair base operations one day.

Ata workshop in October, Pulaski County Committee members proposed formalizing the draft
MPCC/MOU framework into a statutory “Regional Planning Commission” created by a binding
Interlocal Agreement, both expressly authorized by Arkansas Code. Judge Hyde and County
Attorney Adam Fogleman explained to the Committee in its proposal that by converting the
proposed MPCC/MOU approach into one administered by a single agency — a Regional Planning
Commission — that is backed by formal action of each governing body, that 11 jurisdictions
involved would create a streamlined approach that would provide a single regulatory framework

capable of handling all military compatibility and related land use issues on behalf of all the
jurisdictions.

In short, the County’s proposal was simply to convert the Committee’s informal, non-binding
approach into a formalized, consistent and binding one.

The CUSI Project Manager is bringing this forward for the purpose of gaining the Council’s
support to pursue this concept with the project committees with the participation of City staff.
Any decision of whether to enter into an Interlocal Agreement or to participate in a future
Regional Planning Commission — solely for miliary-related purposes — would be the Council’s
decision, at a future date, once a formal framework is developed and brought forward.

The Implementation Committee is at work educating the City Councils and Quorum Courts in
the area on the need for appropriate planning in the proximity of LRAFB and is considering
Pulaski County’s proposal for formalizing this approach.

The Regional Planning Commission:

A Resolution on the RPC before the City Council simply authorizes the Mayor to sign the
Resolution and to appoint a representative of this area to serve on a soon-to-be-formed Regional
Planning Commission. This Regional Planning Commission does not take any authority
away from the city or county Planning Commission. State law prohibits such action. It
merely serves to ensure that the City and County Planning Commissions work together and
consistently guide the unified development of the area as related to the LRAFB.

The Regional Planning Commission:
The Regional Planning Commission will:

*Eliminate planning duplication on issues that may affect the base

*Promote economy and efficiency in the coordinated development of the area
*Serve in an advisory capacity to cities and counties for base-related issues
*Promote the general welfare and prosperity of the people in the affected area

ORDINANCE NO. 3 OF 2023

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND SECTION 28-141 OF THE CODE OF
CABOT; TO REPEAL ANY CONFLICTING LEGISLATION; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, State law in the Advertising and Promotion Commission Act
empowers a city to, among other things, impose a tax on the gross receipts of hotels and
other similar businesses. The revenue generated by said tax is then under the sole
management of that city’s Advertising and Promotion Commission, an independent
commission acting pursuant to state law; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council followed all applicable law and enacted said
tax on the gross receipts of hotels and other similar businesses. This tax was codified in
Section 28-141 of the Code of Cabot; and

WHEREAS, this ordinance does not change or in any way affect the rate of
Advertising and Promotion tax on restaurants and similar businesses; and

WHEREAS, other than the percentage change, the other code changes made by
this ordinance mirror the applicable state statute and are changed herein in order to keep
Cabot’s code consistent with said state statute; and

WHEREAS, the funds collected and managed by the Cabot Advertising and
Promotion Commission are spent on dedicated public purposes and inure to the benefit of
the residents of Cabot. The Cabot City Council wishes to amend Code of Cabot Section
28-141 in order to ensure continued and increased benefits to the residents of Cabot.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Section 28-141 of the Code of Cabot is hereby amended as
delineated in Exhibit “A”, attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, and
the same provisions thereof shall be controlling from the date on which this ordinance
shall take effect. The ordinances establishing Section 28-141 and the content thereof are
likewise amended in the same manner and to the same extent.

SECTION 2: If, for any reason, any portion or portions of this ordinance shall
be held invalid, such invalidity shall in no way affect the remaining portions thereof

which are valid, and that such valid portions shall be and remain in full force and effect.
--- page 7 (OCR) ---
This ordinance is therefore declared to be several.

SECTION 3: All Ordinances, parts of Ordinances, sections of the Code of
Cabot, or parts of sections of the Code of Cabot in conflict with the provisions of this
ordinance and the code amendment mandated herein are hereby repealed to the extent of

the conflict.

ANNUAL OPERATING BUDGET; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

infrastructure improvement project that will be completed under the auspices of the U.S.
Department of Commerce Financial Assistance award grant program authorized by the Cabot City
Council in Resolution 31 of 2022; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to Sec. 2-583 of the Code of Cabot and other applicable law, the
City followed proper procedures to obtain statements of qualifications for engineering and related
services in the above referenced project, and it was determined by the Selection Group that Bond
Consulting Engineers, Inc (Bond) was the most qualified firm to provide those services to the City
of Cabot for that project. In Resolution 6 of 2023, the Cabot City Council affirmed the Selection

WHEREAS, State law in the Advertising and Promotion Commission Act
empowers a city to, among other things, impose a tax on the gross receipts of hotels and
other similar businesses. The revenue generated by said tax is then under the sole
management of that city’s Advertising and Promotion Commission, an independent
commission acting pursuant to state law; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council followed all applicable law and enacted said
tax on the gross receipts of hotels and other similar businesses. This tax was codified in
Section 28-141 of the Code of Cabot; and

WHEREAS, this ordinance does not change or in any way affect the rate of
Advertising and Promotion tax on restaurants and similar businesses; and

WHEREAS, other than the percentage change, the other code changes made by
this ordinance mirror the applicable state statute and are changed herein in order to keep
Cabot’s code consistent with said state statute; and

WHEREAS, the funds collected and managed by the Cabot Advertising and
Promotion Commission are spent on dedicated public purposes and inure to the benefit of
the residents of Cabot. The Cabot City Council wishes to amend Code of Cabot Section
28-141 in order to ensure continued and increased benefits to the residents of Cabot.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Section 28-141 of the Code of Cabot is hereby amended as
delineated in Exhibit “A”, attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, and
the same provisions thereof shall be controlling from the date on which this ordinance
shall take effect. The ordinances establishing Section 28-141 and the content thereof are
likewise amended in the same manner and to the same extent.

SECTION 2: If, for any reason, any portion or portions of this ordinance shall
be held invalid, such invalidity shall in no way affect the remaining portions thereof

which are valid, and that such valid portions shall be and remain in full force and effect.

WHEREAS, the City, in conjunction with Cabot City Beautiful, wishes to conduct
a Household Hazardous Waste Round-up event currently scheduled for March 2023;
and
WHEREAS, given the nature of the services at issue and the unknown factor of how
much hazardous waste will be disposed of, it is impossible to say what the final cost will be
and if the amount will be one that requires competitive bidding to be used; and
WHEREAS Ark. Code Ann § 14-58-303 et al., provides that the governing body may
waive the requirement of competitive bidding in situations where the procedure is deemed not
feasible or practical; and
WHEREAS the service authorized herein - the removal and disposal of household
hazardous waste — is hereby found to be directly beneficial to the health, safety, and welfare of
the people of Cabot.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to enter into
an Agreement with CTS Services, Inc. to collect, bulk, containerize, transfer and recycle/dispose
of household hazardous waste during the Household Hazardous Waste Round-up event. The
agreement is authorized to be consistent with the terms and prices detailed in the attached
Exhibit A. The City Council recognizes that the amount of payment to CTS for these services
will depend on how much and what type of hazardous waste is disposed of at the event.
Payment to CTS is authorized to be consistent with the unit costs listed in Exhibit A.

SECTION 2: Competitive bidding for this matter is hereby deemed to be neither
feasible nor practical given both the time constraints and the nature of the project that makes
fixed pricing, and therefore bidding, extremely difficult. In addition, the scope of the project, the

very large variety of types and forms of hazardous waste that could be collected, and the

RESOLUTION 13 OF 2023

AN RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR AND CITY CLERK~TREASURER
TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH ARKANSAS VALLEY
COMMUNICATIONS FOR POLICE DEPARTMENT RADIOS AND RELATED
EQUIPMENT; TO WAIVE THE COMPETITIVE BIDDING REQUIREMENTS IN
ORDER TO ENTER INTO SAID AGREEMENT; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the Cabot Police Department is in need of new radios and related
equipment; and

WHEREAS, the Police Department’s existing radios and radio infrastructure are
primarily Motorola branded. It is essential for the new radios and related equipment to also be
Motorola branded in order to best work alongside and interface with the existing radio
infrastructure. The optimal working conditions of the Police Department’s radio and related
equipment are of very high importance to public safety. This matter directly impacts the Police
Department’s ability to safely, quickly, and efficiently respond to emergency situations and
therefore directly benefit the health, safety, and welfare of the public; and

WHEREAS, Ark. Code Ann § 14-58-303 provides that the governing body may waive
the requirement of competitive bidding in situations where the procedure is deemed not feasible
or practical; and

WHEREAS, while there are other providers of police radios, Arkansas Valley
Communications (AVC) is the only known licensed provider of Motorola police radios of the
specifications sought by the Police Department in Arkansas. The purchase of licensed radios
from an in-state supplier is of high importance for warranty, repair, and quality control issues. As
such, the Cabot City Council herein finds that it would be neither feasible nor practical to
conduct competitive bidding in this matter; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council supports the Police Department in its purchase of

ORDINANCE NO. 3 OF 2023

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND SECTION 28-141 OF THE CODE OF
CABOT; TO REPEAL ANY CONFLICTING LEGISLATION; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, State law in the Advertising and Promotion Commission Act
empowers a city to, among other things, impose a tax on the gross receipts of hotels and
other similar businesses. The revenue generated by said tax is then under the sole
management of that city’s Advertising and Promotion Commission, an independent
commission acting pursuant to state law; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council followed all applicable law and enacted said
tax on the gross receipts of hotels and other similar businesses. This tax was codified in
Section 28-141 of the Code of Cabot; and

WHEREAS, this ordinance does not change or in any way affect the rate of
Advertising and Promotion tax on restaurants and similar businesses; and

WHEREAS, other than the percentage change, the other code changes made by
this ordinance mirror the applicable state statute and are changed herein in order to keep
Cabot’s code consistent with said state statute; and

WHEREAS, the funds collected and managed by the Cabot Advertising and
Promotion Commission are spent on dedicated public purposes and inure to the benefit of
the residents of Cabot. The Cabot City Council wishes to amend Code of Cabot Section
28-141 in order to ensure continued and increased benefits to the residents of Cabot.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Section 28-141 of the Code of Cabot is hereby amended as
delineated in Exhibit “A”, attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, and
the same provisions thereof shall be controlling from the date on which this ordinance
shall take effect. The ordinances establishing Section 28-141 and the content thereof are
likewise amended in the same manner and to the same extent.

SECTION 2: If, for any reason, any portion or portions of this ordinance shall
be held invalid, such invalidity shall in no way affect the remaining portions thereof

which are valid, and that such valid portions shall be and remain in full force and effect.
--- page 7 (OCR) ---
This ordinance is therefore declared to be several.

SECTION 3: All Ordinances, parts of Ordinances, sections of the Code of
Cabot, or parts of sections of the Code of Cabot in conflict with the provisions of this
ordinance and the code amendment mandated herein are hereby repealed to the extent of

the conflict.

PART II — UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT CODE
ARTICLE IV. — ZONING CODE

Section 4.16 — Food Truck Parks. (Currently not in the UDC)

4.16.1

4.16.2

4.16.3

Purpose and Intent. The purpose and intent of this section is to regulate specific activities
that are commercial in nature while preserving and enhancing the aesthetic beauty of the
city. More specifically, the intent of the food truck park regulations is to:

a. To serve and protect the health, safety and welfare of the general public;

b. To establish a uniform set of rules and regulations that are fair and equitable;

c. To provide economic development opportunities to small entrepreneurs in the city;

d. To promote stable vendors who will enrich the city’s ambiance and be assets to public
security.

Uses. Food Truck Parks shall be permitted on private property as a Special Permit Use in
Commercial and Industrial zoning districts.

Standards. The Planning Commission may approve, deny, defer, or modify a Food Truck
Park site plan based on findings of fact with regard to the standards set forth below. The
appropriateness of these standards shall be determined at the discretion of the Planning
Commission for each specific location. The Planning Commission shall not permit any
Food Truck Park use in a zone as a Special Use that in not permitted under the Zoning
Code.

In carrying out the purpose of this section, the Commission consideration shall include, but
not limited to, the following development standards and design specifics.

The appropriateness of these standards shall be determined at the discretion of the Planning
Commission for each Food Truck Park location.

a. The proposed use is so designed, located and proposed to be operated that the public
health, safety and welfare will be protected.

b. The proposed land use is compatible with and will not adversely affect other property
in the area where it is proposed to be located.

c. The proposed use is within the provisions of “Special Uses” as set out in the Code.

d. The proposed use conforms to all applicable provisions of this Code for the zoning
district for which it is to be located, and the use facilitates public convenience at that
location.

e. The size and shape of the site, and the size, shape and arrangement of the proposed
structures, are in keeping with the intent of the Comprehensive plan and this Code.

f. The ingress or egress, off-street parking, loading and pedestrian ways will be efficient
and safe.

g. Safeguards, including, but not limited to, hours and methods of operation,
landscaping and screening, controlling noxious or offensive emissions, including
lighting, noise, glare, dust and odor, are satisfactory.

h. Landscaping, fencing and open space will be properly maintained by the
owner/developer.

i. Proposed sign(s) will be appropriate for the location and in accordance with the
requirements of the existing City Code.

j. Public utilities are, or will be, available and will not be overloaded.

4.16.2 Procedure for Authorizing.

a. Permit Required: Unless specifically exempted in this Code, it shall be unlawful for
any person to engage in the business of a food truck park unless he/she has first
obtained a Special Permit Use from the Planning Commission. It is the responsibility
of the business owner to verify if a food truck park has been approved for the property
location.

b, Application: Application for a Food Truck Park shall be made by the property owner

or authorized agent for the owner. The application shall be submitted to the Public
Works Office which will process all applicable surveys, site plans and other
supporting information pertinent to this review process.
Notice of a Special Permit Use application shall be published at least one time, not
less than fifteen (15) days prior to the date of the public hearing, in a newspaper of
general circulation. The applicant shall give notice of such hearing by posting a
suitable and pertinent sign, provided by the City, on the property involved not less
than fifteen (15) days prior to the hearing.

c. Site Plan Requirements: The site plan requirements for a Food Truck Park application
shall follow the same requirements as a standard site plan as listed in Zoning Code
section. The Food Truck Park shall meet Off-Street parking requirements, sign
regulations and landscape requirements. The site plan shall also show the following
requirements:

i. The location and size for each food truck vendor pad with appropriate
separation distances;

LOCATED AT 805 WEST MAIN STREET FOR THE CITY’S

WORK THEREFOR; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, in Ordinance 4 of 2023, the City Council Authorized the issuance of Franchise
Fee Revenue Bonds, Series 2023. Per that ordinance, the revenue raised by said bonds would be
used for courts and police facilities; and

WHEREAS, the City proposes to jointly accomplish said courts and police facilities
through the construction of a justice center. The City, as authorized in Resolution 31 of 2021,
acquired the real property located at 805 West Main Street in Cabot. The City Council herein
finds that said property would be proper and appropriate to be utilized as the proposed justice
center; and

WHEREAS, the City underwent the proper legal procedures for the selection of a
professional service provide, and, as authorized by Resolution 8 of 2020, the City entered into
an agreement with Halff to provide engineering services and said agreement provides for the
continued provision of engineering services to the City on an as needed basis. It is herein
acknowledged that Halff often utilizes WDD for the architectural component of their services
and that both companies provided good service to the City previously. As such, the City is
authorized to utilize Halff for the needed preliminary design and engineering services for the
proposed justice center; and

WHEREAS, the City Council acknowledges that agreements for construction services
and other appropriate services will be brought before it as appropriate when the preliminary
design work has been readied; and

WHEREAS, the City Council wishes to authorize the use of the property located at 805

West Main Street for the proposed justice center and further authorizes the preliminary design
and engineering services.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The Cabot City Council herein grants its authorization to utilize the real
property located at 805 West Main Street in Cabot for the proposed justice center. The Mayor
and City Clerk~Treasurer are authorized, pursuant both to this resolution and to Resolution 8

of 2020, to utilize Halff for preliminary design and engineering services for the proposed justice

to a Fire Department Connection (FDC).

AND
ESTABLISHING ITS AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITIES

This Intergovernmental Agreement is made and entered into this__ day of
____, 2023, among parties City of Jacksonville, Pulaski County, City of North
Little Rock, City of Sherwood, City of Maumelle, City of Cabot, City of Ward, City of
Austin, Lonoke County, Faulkner County and White County pursuant to Ark. Code
Ann. §§ 14-14-910, 14-56-501 et seq. and 14-17-301 et seq. to create the Little Rock
Air Force Base Regional Planning Committee and to establish its authority and

responsibilities.

WHEREAS, Little Rock Air Force Base (“LRAFB”), the Local Governments,
and the community have historically cooperated to ensure the sustainability of the
ongoing mission of LRAFB and its associated local installations, as well as the

preservation of quality of life for citizens and businesses in the region; and

| WHEREAS, the ongoing presence and operation of LRAFB is critical to the
nation’s defense, the protection and well-being of the citizens of Arkansas, and to

the common good of this community; and

WHEREAS, for more than three (8) years representatives and community

members of these participating jurisdictions have been actively meeting on a

regular basis in pursuit of developing appropriate recommendations to ensure that
land uses around the Little Rock Air Force Base and other mission critical sites
(hereinafter “Base” or “LRAFB”) are compatible with the missions of the Base.

These meetings produced the LRAFB Compatible Use Study.

WHEREAS, the 2021 Little Rock Air Force Base Compatible Use Study (the
LRAFB Compatible Use Study) recognized the importance of the ongoing input of

community members affected by military land uses.

WHEREAS, the LRAFB Compatible Use Study was a regional initiative,
managed by the City of Jacksonville, initiated by the Office of Military Affairs in the
Arkansas Economic Development Commission and the participating jurisdictions to

identify and mitigate land use compatibility concerns.

WHEREAS, during the development of the LRAFB Compatible Use Study,
the parties to this agreement participated in the development of a uniform regional
military zoning ordinance and administrative procedures for effectuating

coordination among the parties.

WHEREAS, following the 2021 Compatible Use Study, the parties
participated in the development of a compatible use implementation program from
July 2022 until its completion in February 2023, including development of the final

report: CUS Phase II: Implementation for Little Rock Air Force Base and Environs.
--- page 54 (OCR) ---
WHEREAS, the participating jurisdictions have a uniform goal of securing
and sustaining LRAFB’s economically significant military training and operational

missions while simultaneously promoting and ensuring compatible growth.

WHEREAS, the Parties to this Agreement wish to implement these and
other recommendations in the 2021 LRAFB Compatible Use Study in order to

establish a consistent regulatory and coordination framework for the lands around

LRAFB.

WHEREAS, the distribution and division of authority between cities and
counties regarding growth planning and land use controls is complex, and
complexities may be resolved or avoided with the centralization of expertise and
record keeping, a coordination framework, and, within Pulaski County’s

unincorporated areas, as provided herein, the administration of a County Military

Zoning Overlay (MZO).

WHEREAS, a regional planning commission will ensure that participating
jurisdictions are equally represented, promote consistent application of uniform
provisions of code, eliminate duplication, promote economy and efficiency in the
coordinated development of the area, and promote the general welfare and

prosperity of the people.

WHEREAS, the parties to this agreement have determined, after years of

study and coordination, that the agreement represents an authorized and effective

means of complying with Ark. Code Ann. § 14-56-426, Control of Property Use —

ALL OF THE PARTIES HERETO AS FOLLOWS:
SECTION 1: PURPOSE

This Intergovernmental Agreement is executed pursuant to Ark. Code Ann. §
14-14-910 to provide for formal cooperative action between the parties hereto and
for the coordination of land use and development planning in the area surrounding
the LRAFB to ensure that current and future land uses are compatible with the
current and future operation and missions of the LRAFB, in the manner set out

herein.

A further purpose of this Agreement is to maintain a uniform, consistent, and
effective approach to protecting LRAFB installations from encroachment and
incompatible land uses for the long-term through the administration of Military

Zoning Overlay ordinances , as well as through awareness and public outreach.

The division of land area into MZO Area and Advisory Areas jurisdictions is
designed to comport with the expressions of willingness of representatives of the
Participating Jurisdictions to participate in accordance with this Agreement
through mechanisms most fitting and appropriate to each jurisdiction’s needs and

authorities.

SECTION 2: NAME
--- page 56 (OCR) ---
The name of the organization created by this agreement shall be “Little Rock

Air Force Base Regional Planning Committee.”
SECTION 3: ORGANIZATION

a. The Little Rock Air Force Base Regional Planning Committee (“Committee”)
shall be authorized by this agreement to make determinations,
recommendations, and to take other actions for the purpose of ensuring land
development and use compatibility with LRAFB activities, as provided
herein.

b. Military Zoning Ordinance (MZO) Areas — The MZO Areas include the
jurisdictions of those local governments that have an adopted MZO,
consistent with the regional Military Zoning Ordinance included as an
appendix to the CUS Phase II: Implementation for Little Rock Air Force Base
and Environs final report. Figure A, below, lists the Participating
Jurisdictions confirmed or committed to joining the RPC as an MZO Area
jurisdiction and the parties’ agreed to allocation of powers and authorities
among the MZO jurisdictions, as authorized by Arkansas law, including Ark.
Code Ann. § 14-56-426, Control of Property Use — Proximity to Military
Installation. The MZO Areas may be modified, following approval of the RPC
membership, through adoption of an ordinance by a party hereto indicating
the jurisdiction’s desire to thereafter be member of the RPC as an MZO Area

jurisdiction.
--- page 57 (OCR) ---
c. Advisory Areas — The Advisory Areas include the jurisdictions of those local
governments that have not adopted an MZO. Figure A lists the Participating
Jurisdictions confirmed or committed to joining the RPC as an Advisory Area
jurisdiction only. The RPC’s role with respect to Advisory Area jurisdictions
is advisory only and its determinations are not binding on the Advisory Area
jurisdiction. The Advisory Areas may be modified, following approval of the
RPC membership, through adoption of an ordinance by a party hereto
indicating the jurisdiction’s desire to thereafter be member of the RPC as an
Advisory Area jurisdiction. Advisory Area jurisdictions shall use outreach
and public awareness materials developed by the RPC in coordination with
LRAFB and the Participating Jurisdictions, including, for example, those
included as appendices to the CUS Phase II: Implementation for Little Rock
Air Force Base and Environs final report.

d. Participating Jurisdiction — A Participating Jurisdiction is a city or county
identified herein, which has adopted an ordinance through its governing body
authorizing its executive officer to execute this Agreement, and the same
executive officer has done so. Each Participating Jurisdictions shall be
designated as MZO or Advisory Area jurisdictions.

e. Military Zoning Overlays (MZOs) — The code of land use controls, adopted by
ordinance by an MZO Area jurisdiction, consistent with the regional MZO
included as an appendix in the CUS Phase II: Implementation for Little Rock

Air Force Base and Environs final report, which was jointly developed by the
--- page 58 (OCR) ---
Participating Jurisdictions, Little Rock Air Force Base, and other relevant
agencies and stakeholders. At the time of entry into this Intergovernmental
Agreement, none of the Participating Jurisdictions will have adopted a
Military Zoning Overlay; however, it is anticipated that each Participating
Jurisdiction will adopt such a code, or incorporate into their existing code, the
same or materially consistent protections intended to meet the ends
described in the regional MZO.

Upon the execution of this Agreement, each Participating Jurisdiction shall
be entitled to appoint or elect one (1) member to the RPC, and in the same

Report on the Audit of the Financial Statements
Opinions

We have audited the regulatory basis financial statements of the City of Cabot, Arkansas (City), which are comprised of the
Balance Sheet — Regulatory Basis for the general fund, street fund, and other funds in the aggregate as of December 31,
2021, and the related Statements of Revenues, Expenses, and Changes in Fund Balances and Budget and Actual — General
and Street Funds — Regulatory Basis for the year then ended, and the related notes to the financial statements.

Unmodified Opinions on Regulatory Basis of Accounting

In our opinion, the accompanying regulatory basis financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects,
the regulatory basis financial position of the general fund, street fund, and other funds in the aggregate of the City of Cabot,
Arkansas, as of December 31, 2021; the regulatory basis revenues, expenditures, and changes in net position; and the budgetary
comparisons for the general fund and street fund for the year then ended, in accordance with the financial reporting provisions
of Ark. Code Ann. § 10-4-412 described in Note 1.

Adverse Opinion on U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles

In our opinion, because of the significance of the matter discussed in the Basis for Adverse Opinion on U.S. Generally
Accepted Accounting Principles section of our report, the accompanying regulatory basis financial statements referred to above
do not present fairly, in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, the financial
position of the general fund, street fund, and other funds in the aggregate of the City of Cabot, Arkansas, as of December 31,
2021, or the revenues, expenditures, and changes in net position and, where applicable, cash flows thereof for the year then
ended.

Basis for Opinions

We conducted our audit in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the United States of America (GAAS)
and the standards applicable to financial audits contained in Government Auditing Standards, issued by the Comptroller
General of the United States. Our responsibilities under those standards are further described in the Auditor's Responsibilities
for the Audit of the Regulatory Basis Financial Statements section of our report. We are required to be independent of the
City, and to meet our other ethical responsibilities, in accordance with the relevant ethical requirements relating to our audit.
We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinions.

Basis for Adverse Opinion on U.S, Generally Accepted Accounting Principles

As described in Note 1 of the financial statements, the financial statements are prepared by the City on the basis of the
financial reporting provisions of Ark. Code Ann. § 10-4412, which is a basis of accounting other than accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States of America, to meet the requirements permitted by the State of Arkansas.

The effects on the financial statements of the variances between the regulatory basis of accounting described in Note 1 and
accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, although not reasonably determinable, are presumed
to be material and pervasive.

Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting

In planning and performing our audit of the financial statements, we considered the City’s internal control over financial
reporting (internal control) as a basis for designing audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances for the purpose
of expressing our opinions on the financial statements, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness
of the Gity's internal control. Accordingly, we do not express an opinion on the effectiveness of the City's internal control.

A deficiency in internal control exists when the design or operation of a control does not allow management or employees, in
the normal course of performing their assigned functions, to prevent, or detect and correct, misstatements on a timely basis.
A material weakness is a deficiency, or a combination of deficiencies, in internal control, such that there is a reasonable
possibility that a material misstatement of the entity's financial statements will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on
a timely basis. A significant deficiency is a deficiency, or a combination of deficiencies, in internal control that is less severe
than a material weakness, yet important enough to merit attention by those charged with governance.

Our consideration of internal control was for the limited purpose described in the first paragraph of this section and was not
designed to identify all deficiencies in internal control that might be material weaknesses or significant deficiencies. Given
these limitations, during our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internat control that we consider to be material
weaknesses. However, material weaknesses or significant deficiencies may exist that were not identified.

Summary of Significant Accounting Policies

A.

Financial Reporting Entity

The City of Cabot was incorporated under the laws of the State of Arkansas and operates under an elected
Mayor-Council form of government. The reporting entity includes all funds of the City. Under accounting
principles generally accepted in the United States of America (GAAP) as established by the Government
Accounting Standards Board, the following funds of the City would have been included in the reporting entity:
Water and Wastewater Department, Advertising and Promotion Commission, and Parks and Recreation
Commission. However, under Arkansas's regulatory basis described below, inclusion of these funds is not
required and these funds are not included in this report.

Basis of Presentation — Regulatory

The financial statements are presented in accordance with the regulatory basis of presentation as prescribed
or permitted by Ark. Code Ann. § 10-4-412. The law requires that the financial statements be presented on
a fund basis with, as a minimum, the general fund and street fund presented separately with all other funds
included in the financial statements presented in the aggregate. This law also stipulates that the financial
statements consist of a balance sheet; a statement of revenues, expenditures, and changes in fund balances;
a comparison of the final adopted budget to the actual expenditures for the general and street funds; notes
to financial statements; and a supplemental schedule of capital assets.

The. regulatory basis of presentation is not in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles
(GAAP). GAAP require that basic financial statements present government-wide and fund financial
statements. Additionally, GAAP require the following major concepts: Management's Discussion and
Analysis, separate financial statements for fiduciary fund types and other requirements for fiduciary fund
types, specific procedures for the identification of major governmental funds, and applicable note disclosures.
The regulatory basis of presentation does not require government-wide financial statements or the previously
identified concepts.

A fund is defined as a fiscal and accounting entity with a self-balancing set of accounts recording cash and
other financial resources, together with related liabilities and residual balances, and changes therein, which
are segregated for purposes of carrying on specific activities or attaining certain objectives in accordance
with special regulations, restrictions, or limitations.

The following types of funds are recognized in the accompanying regulatory basis financial statements.

General Fund - The General Fund is used to account for and report all financial resources not accounted for
and reported in another fund.

Street Fund - The Street Fund (Special Revenue Fund) is used to account for and report the proceeds of
specific revenue sources that are restricted or committed to expenditure for specified purposes other than
debt service or capital projects. The Street Fund accounts for and reports the proceeds of state highway
turnback and property taxes that are restricted or committed for maintaining and constructing highways and
streets.

Other Funds in the Aggregate - Other Funds in the Aggregate consist of all funds included in the financial
statements except for the General and Street Funds. The following types of funds are included in this column
as follows:

Special Revenue Funds - Special Revenue Funds are used to account for and report the proceeds of
specific revenue sources that are restricted or committed to expenditure for specified purposes other
than debt service or capital projects. See Schedules 1 and 2 for Special Revenue Funds as reported
with other funds in the aggregate.

Capital Projects Funds - Capital Projects Funds are used to account for and report financial resources
that are restricted, committed, or assigned to expenditure for capital outlay, including the acquisition or
construction of capital facilities and other capital assets. See Schedules 1 and 2 for Capital Projects
Funds as reported with other funds in the aggregate.

C. Basis of Accounting - Regulatory

The financial statements are prepared on the regulatory basis of accounting as prescribed or permitted by
Ark. Code Ann. § 10-4-412. This regulatory basis differs from accounting principles generally accepted in
the United States of America. Revenues generally are recognized as soon as they are both measurable and
available. Revenues are considered to be available when they are collectible within the current period or
soon enough thereafter to pay liabilities of the current period. For this purpose, the government considers
revenues to be available if they are collected within 60 days of the end of the current period. However, most
state aid received from the State Treasury is by state law revenue of the year in which it was received by the
government. Expenditures generally are recorded when a liability is incurred. Liabilities incurred by the
government on or before the end of the current period that are paid within 60 days of the end of the current
period, are considered to be expenditures of the current period. However, debt service expenditures, as well
as expenditures related to compensated absences and claims and judgments, are recorded only when
payment is due. As a result of the use of this regulatory basis of accounting, capital assets and long-term
debt are not recorded in these financial statements. Pension trust funds are reported in a separate column
as a part of supplementary information in order to provide users a better understanding of the entity as a
whole.

The regulatory basis of accounting is not in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles
(GAAP). GAAP require the following major concepts: Accrual basis of accounting for government-wide
financial statements, including depreciation expense, modified accrual basis of accounting for fund financial
statements, separate identification of special and extraordinary items, inclusion of capital assets and debt in
the financial statements, inclusion of the net pension liability in the financial statements, and applicable note
disclosures. The regulatory basis of accounting does not require the previously identified concepts.

G. Fund Balance Classification Policies and Procedures

The Municipality's highest level of decision-making authority is its City Council. The establishment of amounts
classified as committed fund balances and any subsequent modifications to such balances are the result of
formal action taken by the City Council through passage of an ordinance. The City Council is authorized to
assign amounts to a specific purpose, although a formal policy has not been established.

The Municipality does not have a policy addressing whether it considers restricted or unrestricted amounts
to have been spent when an expenditure is incurred for purposes for which both restricted and unrestricted
amounts are available. For classification of fund balance amounts, restricted resources are considered spent
before unrestricted. The Municipality does not have a policy addressing which resources to use within the
unrestricted fund balance when committed, assigned, or unassigned fund balances are available. When
expenditures are incurred for purposes for which amounts in any of the unrestricted fund balance
classifications could be used, committed amounts are reduced first, followed by assigned amounts, and then

The City is exposed to various risks of loss related to torts; theft of, damage to, and destruction of assets; errors
and omissions; and natural disasters. These risks are covered by commercial insurance purchased from
independent third parties and participation in a public entity risk pool. The amount of settlements, if any, has not
exceeded the insurance coverage for each of the past three years. There were no significant reductions in
insurance coverage in the major categories of risk from coverage in the prior year.

The City has workers compensation insurance with JTS Financial Services.

The City participates in the Arkansas Municipal League Program (public entity risk pools) for coverage in the
following areas:

Municipal Vehicle Program

A. Liability - This program may pay all sums the municipality legally must pay as damages because of
bodily injury, death or property damage to which this agreement applies involving a covered municipal
vehicle and for which the municipality is liable. The limit of payment by the program is as follows:
$25,000 because of bodily injury to or death of one person in any one accident; $50,000 because of
bodily injury to or death of two or more persons in any one accident; and $25,000 because of injury to
or destruction of property of others in any one accident. The City shall pay into the program each year
a charge established annually by the program administrator for covered municipal vehicles and self-
propelled mobile equipment owned or leased by the City.

Funding Policy

The employee contribution rate depends on the type of service being rendered and whether or not the service is

C. Volunteer fire service: no employee contribution

The City is required to contribute at an actuarially determined rate. The contribution requirements of plan members
are established and may be amended by State law. The contribution requirements of the City are established and
may be amended by the LOPF! Board of Trustees. The plan is also funded with state insurance tax. The City’s
contribution to the plan was $908,162 and the amount of insurance tax paid by the state to the plan for the benefit
of the City was $417,779 for the year ended December 31, 2021.

Plan Description

coverage under this System. APERS, administered by a Board of Trustees, provides retirement and disability
benefits, annual cost-of-living adjustments, and death benefits to plan members and beneficiaries. Benefit
provisions are established by State law and can be amended only by the Arkansas General Assembly. The
Arkansas Public Employees Retirement System issues a publicly available financial report that includes financiat
statements and required supplementary information for APERS. That report may be obtained by writing to
Arkansas Public Employees Retirement System, 124 W. Capitol, Suite 400, Little Rock, Arkansas 72201, by calling
4-800-682-7377, or on their website www.apers.org.

Funding Policy

APERS has contributory and non-contributory plans. Contributory members are required by State law to contribute
5% of their salary. Each participating employer is required by State law to contribute at a rate established by the
Board of Trustees of the system, based on the annual actuarial valuation. The City’s contribution to the plan was
$776,971 for the year ended June 30, 2021.

Clerk/Treasurer Retirement Benefits
Plan Description

Ark. Code Ann. § 24-12-121 establishes retirement benefits for clerk/treasurers in cities of the first class and death
benefits to their spouses at the option of the governing body of the City. Benefits and contribution provisions are
established by State law and can be amended only by the Arkansas General Assembly. A retiree is entitled to
receive a monthly retirement benefit during the remainder of their natural life, a sum equal to one-half (1/2) of the
monthly salary received during the last preceding year of service. Retirement benefits are to be paid from the
City’s General Fund. A clerk/treasurer may retire: 1.) upon reaching the age of 60 with a minimum of 10 years of
service or 2.) upon serving 20 years, regardless of age. The City paid former Clerk/Treasurers $58,557 for the
year ended December 31, 2021.

ORDINANCE NO. 6 OF 2023
AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND SECTION 4.16 OF THE UNIFIED
DEVELOPMENT CODE OF THE CODE OF CABOT; TO DECLARE AN
EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, it is the desire of the Cabot Planning Commission to amend Article
IV of the Unified Development Code (“UDC”), Section 4.16 as delineated in Exhibit “A”
attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, subject to the approval of this
governing body; and

WHEREAS, state law empowers municipalities to adopt ordinances to provide for
the safety, health, comfort, and convenience of inhabitants of the city; therefore, the
purposes for the amendment to the UDC are to carry out and protect various elements of
the Comprehensive Development Plan and all other adopted plans and policies of the
City of Cabot and to promote the safety, order, convenience, prosperity, and general
welfare of the citizens of Cabot. The Cabot City Council hereby finds that the
amendments approved of herein promote and further all of said purposes.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Article IV, Section 4.16 of the Unified Development Code
(“UDC”) of the Code of Cabot, is hereby amended, as delineated in Exhibit “A” attached
hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, and the same provisions thereof shall be
controlling from the date on which this ordinance shall take effect.

SECTION 2: If, for any reason, any portion or portions of this ordinance shall
be held invalid, such invalidity shall in no way affect the remaining portions thereof
which are valid, and that such valid portions shall be and remain in full force and effect.

SECTION 3: Any portion or portions of the amendments to the UDC adopted

herein which are contrary to existing Ordinances of the City of Cabot, Arkansas shall
prevail, and all Ordinances or parts of Ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby

repealed to the extent of the conflict.

SECTION 4: EMERGENCY. The provisions of the Unified Development Code
are of significant importance to the safety and welfare of the residents of Cabot. These code
amendments will lead to better and more consistent enforcement of the UDC and promote
more uniform compliance. Additionally, this governing body herein finds that this ordinance
will inure to the health, safety, and welfare of the residents of Cabot. The sooner these
amendments can become effective, the sooner the benefits to public safety and welfare will
accrue. An emergency is therefore declared and this Ordinance being necessary for the
preservation of the public peace, health, safety, and welfare shall be in full force and effect

from and after its passage.

Section 4.16 — Food Truck Parks. (Currently not in the UDC)

4.16.1

4.16.2

4.16.3

Purpose and Intent. The purpose and intent of this section is to regulate specific activities
that are commercial in nature while preserving and enhancing the aesthetic beauty of the
city. More specifically, the intent of the food truck park regulations is to:

a. To serve and protect the health, safety and welfare of the general public;

b. To establish a uniform set of rules and regulations that are fair and equitable;

c. To provide economic development opportunities to small entrepreneurs in the city;

d. To promote stable vendors who will enrich the city’s ambiance and be assets to public
security.

Uses. Food Truck Parks shall be permitted on private property as a Special Permit Use in
Commercial and Industrial zoning districts.

Standards. The Planning Commission may approve, deny, defer, or modify a Food Truck
Park site plan based on findings of fact with regard to the standards set forth below. The
appropriateness of these standards shall be determined at the discretion of the Planning
Commission for each specific location. The Planning Commission shall not permit any
Food Truck Park use in a zone as a Special Use that in not permitted under the Zoning
Code.

In carrying out the purpose of this section, the Commission consideration shall include, but
not limited to, the following development standards and design specifics.

The appropriateness of these standards shall be determined at the discretion of the Planning
Commission for each Food Truck Park location.

a. The proposed use is so designed, located and proposed to be operated that the public
health, safety and welfare will be protected.

b. The proposed land use is compatible with and will not adversely affect other property
in the area where it is proposed to be located.

c. The proposed use is within the provisions of “Special Uses” as set out in the Code.

d. The proposed use conforms to all applicable provisions of this Code for the zoning
district for which it is to be located, and the use facilitates public convenience at that
location.

e. The size and shape of the site, and the size, shape and arrangement of the proposed
structures, are in keeping with the intent of the Comprehensive plan and this Code.

f. The ingress or egress, off-street parking, loading and pedestrian ways will be efficient
and safe.

g. Safeguards, including, but not limited to, hours and methods of operation,
landscaping and screening, controlling noxious or offensive emissions, including
lighting, noise, glare, dust and odor, are satisfactory.

h. Landscaping, fencing and open space will be properly maintained by the
owner/developer.

i. Proposed sign(s) will be appropriate for the location and in accordance with the
requirements of the existing City Code.

4.16.2 Procedure for Authorizing.

a. Permit Required: Unless specifically exempted in this Code, it shall be unlawful for
any person to engage in the business of a food truck park unless he/she has first
obtained a Special Permit Use from the Planning Commission. It is the responsibility
of the business owner to verify if a food truck park has been approved for the property
location.

b, Application: Application for a Food Truck Park shall be made by the property owner

or authorized agent for the owner. The application shall be submitted to the Public
Works Office which will process all applicable surveys, site plans and other
supporting information pertinent to this review process.
Notice of a Special Permit Use application shall be published at least one time, not
less than fifteen (15) days prior to the date of the public hearing, in a newspaper of
general circulation. The applicant shall give notice of such hearing by posting a
suitable and pertinent sign, provided by the City, on the property involved not less
than fifteen (15) days prior to the hearing.

c. Site Plan Requirements: The site plan requirements for a Food Truck Park application
shall follow the same requirements as a standard site plan as listed in Zoning Code
section. The Food Truck Park shall meet Off-Street parking requirements, sign
regulations and landscape requirements. The site plan shall also show the following
requirements:

i. The location and size for each food truck vendor pad with appropriate
separation distances;
ii, The permanent utility connections for each food truck space. This shall
include permanent water, sanitary sewer and electricity connections;
iii. The location and size of any proposed permanent structures;
iv. The location of existing and proposed fire hydrants;
y. The location of on-site lighting for the food truck park;
vi. The location of on-site dumpster with an opaque enclosure;
vii. The location of the proposed structure to house restrooms and hand washing
facilities;
viii. Other information staff deems necessary for the site location.

d. Plan Review: The Food Truck Park site plan shall be reviewed through the Public
Works office and the staff shall report to the Planning Commission on its relation and
probable effect on the surrounding area as well as its compliance with the
requirements of this Code.

e. Planning Commission Action: The Planning Commission shall review each Food
Truck Park site plan at its regularly scheduled monthly meeting, at which time
interested person may appear and offer information in support of, or against the
proposed Food Truck Park. The Planning Commission shall review the site plan
based on circumstances of the proposed Food Truck Park including, but not limited
to the location of the park, the size of the lot which the park is proposed, the types of
--- page 10 (OCR) ---
surrounding land uses and the proximity to the park, parking, and any other potential
impacts on public health, safety and welfare.

The Planning Commission shall then make one of the following determinations:
approve the Food Truck Park site plan as requested; approve the Food Truck Park
site plan with modifications; defer the Food Truck Park site plan; or deny the Food
Truck Park site plan.

The Planning Commission may impose conditions and restrictions upon the premises
as may be necessary to reduce or minimize the injurious effects of the Food Truck
Park, ensure compatibility with the surrounding property and carry out the general
intent of the Comprehensive Plan, appropriate neighborhood plans and this Code.

In no case shall the Planning Commission authorize reduction from the minimum
requirements of the code relating to height, area, parking or screening. However, the
applicant may be directed to the Board of Adjustment for variances under the Zoning
Code.

jf. Appeal: Any applicant or other affected party aggrieved by a decision of the Planning
Commission as it relates to the Food Truck Park process shall have the right to appeal
to the City Council. Such appeal must be filed in writing with the City Clerk-
Treasurer within thirty (30) days after the Planning Commission takes final action on
such request. The City Council may affirm, modify, or deny said appealed action of
the Planning Commission.

g. Status of Conditions: Once any portion of the Food Truck Park Special Permit Use
which has been authorized is utilized, all such conditions pertaining to such
authorization shall become immediately operative. The violation of any condition so
imposed shall constitute grounds for revocation of the Food Truck Park Special
Permit Use. Such conditions may include time limits for exercise of such
authorization and must commence within a reasonable time.

The Board of Adjustment is not authorized to grant a variance from conditions
imposed by the commission in connection with the Food Truck Park Special Permit
Use. However, the Board of Adjustment may grant variances as provided by the
Zoning Code.

Amendments or major changes to a Food Truck Park site plan authorization must
follow the same process as the original Food Truck Park site plan. No building permit
shall be issued except in conformance with the provisions of this section.

A Food Truck Park requires a Special Permit Use which is part of the Zoning Code
and shall run with the land upon which the use is located.

4.16.3 Fees. Before any action shall be taken as provided in this section, the applicant shall deposit
with the City an application fee as established or may hereafter be adopted by resolution
of the City Council. Under no condition shall said sum or any part thereof be refunded for
failure of said permit to be approved by the Planning Commission.

All food truck parks shall be located on property that is a legally platted subdivision.
The minimum paved area for each proposed food truck & trailer vendor parking
pad shall be thirty-five (35) by fifteen (15) feet. This area shall not include any
parking spaces that are reserved, encumbered, or designated to satisfy the off-street
parking requirements.

The building design standards in Section 4.9.23 of the Zoning code shall apply to
any permanent structure on the site. These standards do not apply to individual food
truck and trailer vendors.

The property owner, or his/her designated manager, of the food truck park shall be
responsible for the orderly organization of all food truck and trailer vendors, the
cleanliness of the park, and the park’s compliance with all rules and regulations.
The number of food truck and trailer vendors spaces allowed shall be calculated at
one (1) vendor space per 1,000 square feet of lot space. The minimum number of
vendor spaces shall be two (2) and the maximum number of vendor spaces allowed
on any site shall be limited to ten (10).

Only one (1) food truck and trailer vendor are permitted to occupy a vendor space
at the food truck park.

No food truck and trailer vendor, permanent structures, or seating areas shall be
located within the required building setbacks of the applicable zoning district.

The minimum separation between each individual food truck and trailer vendor,
and the minimum separation between any food truck and trailer and a permanent
on-site structure shall be a minimum of ten (10) feet.

A food truck and trailer vendor shall remain outside of a required fire lane, be
located a minimum of three (3) feet from any fire hydrant and shall not block access
to a Fire Department Connection (FDC).

No vehicle drive-through services shall be permitted within a food truck park.
During hours of operation, each food truck and trailer vendor shall be responsible
for providing a trash receptacle for use by customers and shall ensure the area is
kept clear of Litter and debris at all times. A common dumpster may be provided
within the food truck park if the dumpster is screened in accordance with the
screening requirements.

Any food truck park may establish or utilize a permanent structure for indoor
seating, entertainment venue, or similar purposes provided the structures comply
with all applicable requirements, including but not limited to building and fire
department requirements.

Section 5.5.2 Boundary/Perimeter Street Improvements-Current Code

In all subdivisions, developments subject to Site Plan Review, and developments
approved as Planned Unit Developments, the developer shall be required to install, at his/her
expense, boundary street improvements in accordance with the provisions of this subsection.

The City Treasurer's office shall be responsible for receiving, recording, depositing, and
reporting in-lieu cash contributions as may be required from time-to-time. The City Treasurer's
office shall maintain a boundary street improvement account and shall furnish a yearly report
summarizing the account to the Mayor and City Council. This report shall include both the
principal and interest earned for the accounting period.

a. Exempted Developments.

i. Subdivisions, developments subject to Site Plan Review, and developments
approved as Planned Unit Developments along a State or U.S. Highway that is not
slated for improvements as designated on the Statewide Transportation
Improvement Program or Metroplan Transportation Improvement Program shall
be exempt from the provisions and requirements of Section 5.5.2, excluding the
right-of-way dedication provisions.

ii. Subdivisions of four (4) lots or less in residential zones intended for single-family

or two-family dwelling use shall be exempt from the provisions and requirements
of Section 5.5.2, excluding the right-of-way dedication provisions.

b. Improvements Included. Boundary street improvements shall include the following:

i. Reconstruction of one-half section of the abutting street if the existing street does
not meet city standards.

ii. Widening of one-half section of the abutting street to city standards.

iii. Widening, turn-lane improvements, intersection improvements, or signalization as
may be determined to be necessary by a traffic impact analysis of the effects of the
development.

iv. Reconstruction or construction of the entire street section if the existing street does
not meet city standards, and is located wholly within the proposed subdivision or
development.

v. Curb and gutter for the length of the property that adjoins the street.

vi. Drainage piping and drainage structures in accordance with city standards.

vii. One hundred (100) percent of bridge and box culvert construction along local and
collector streets.

viii. Other standard roadway or drainage improvements required by ordinance or as
may be required to conform to accepted engineering practices, as identified by the
City Engineer.

ix. Sidewalks or other bike and pedestrian infrastructure, as otherwise required by this
code.

Subpart D - Post Federal Award Requirements

§200.334 Retention requirements for records.

Financial records, supporting documents, statistical
records, and all other non-Federal entity records
pertinent to a Federal award must be retained for a
period of three years from the date of submission
of the final expenditure report or, for Federal
awards that are renewed quarterly or annually,
from the date of the submission of the quarterly or
annual financial report, respectively, as reported to
the Federal awarding agency or pass-through entity
in the case of a subrecipient. Federal awarding
agencies and pass-through entities must not impose
any other record retention requirements upon non-
Federal entities. The only exceptions are the
following:

(a) If any litigation, claim, or audit is started before
the expiration of the 3-year period, the records
must be retained until all litigation, claims, or audit
findings involving the records have been resolved
and final action taken.

(b) When the non-Federal entity is notified in
writing by the Federal awarding agency, cognizant
agency for audit, oversight agency for audit,
cognizant agency for indirect costs, or pass-
through entity to extend the retention period.

(c) Records for real property and equipment
acquired with Federal funds must be retained for 3
years after final disposition.

(d) When records are transferred to or maintained
by the Federal awarding agency or pass-through
entity, the 3-year retention requirement is not
applicable to the non-Federal entity.

(e) Records for program income transactions after
the period of performance. In some cases
recipients must report program income after the
period of performance. Where there is such a
requirement, the retention period for the records
pertaining to the earning of the program income
starts from the end of the non-Federal entity's
fiscal year in which the program income is earned.

(f) Indirect cost rate proposals and cost allocations
plans. This paragraph applies to the following
types of documents and their supporting records:
Indirect cost rate computations or proposals, cost
allocation plans, and any similar accounting
computations of the rate at which a particular
group of costs is chargeable (such as computer

75

usage chargeback rates or composite fringe benefit
rates).

(1) if submitted for negotiation. If — the
proposal, plan, or other computation is
required to be submitted to the Federal
Government (or to the pass-through entity) to
form the basis for negotiation of the rate, then
the 3-year retention period for its supporting
records starts from the date of such
submission.

(2) Uf not submitted for negotiation. If the
proposal, plan, or other computation is not
required to be submitted to the Federal
Government (or to the pass-through entity) for
negotiation purposes, then the 3-year retention
period for the proposal, plan, or computation
and its supporting records starts from the end
of the fiscal year (or other accounting period)
covered by the proposal, plan, or other
computation.

§200.335 Requests for transfer of records.

The Federal awarding agency must request transfer
of certain records to its custody from the non-
Federal entity when it determines that the records
possess long-term retention value. However, in
order to avoid duplicate recordkeeping, the Federal
awarding agency may make arrangements for the
non-Federal entity to retain any records that are
continuously needed for joint use.

§200.336 Methods for collection, transmission,
and storage of information.

The Federal awarding agency and the non-Federal
entity should, whenever practicable, collect,
transmit, and store Federal award-related
information in open and machine-readable formats
rather than in closed formats or on paper in
accordance with applicable legislative
requirements. A machine-readable format is a
format in a standard computer language (not
English text) that can be read automatically by a
web browser or computer system. The Federal
awarding agency or pass-through entity must
always provide or accept paper versions of Federal
award-related information to and from the non-
Federal entity upon request. If paper copies are
submitted, the Federal awarding agency or pass-
through entity must not require more than an
original and two copies. When original records are
