 CONSULTANT SELECTION PROCEDURES

Section I – Application (These procedures do not apply to Design-Build
Contracts.)

 These procedures apply to federally and state funded contracts for engineering
and design related services for projects and are issued to ensure that a qualified
consultant is obtained through an equitable qualifications-based selection procurement
process and that the prescribed work is properly accomplished in a timely manner at a
fair and reasonable cost.

 Engineering and design related services are defined in 23 Code of Federal
Regulations (CFR) Part 172 to include program management, construction
management, preliminary engineering, design engineering, surveying mapping, or
architectural related services with respect to a highway construction project.
These services also include professional services of an architectural or engineering
nature, as defined by State law, which are required to or may logically or justifiably be
performed or approved by a person licensed, registered, or certified to provide the
services with respect to a highway construction project. Contracts for these services
that are paid with Federal-aid highway program (FAHP) funding will be awarded
following these selection procedures.

 The federal laws and regulations that govern the procurement of engineering and
design related services with FAHP funds are:

  23 United States Code (U.S.C.) 106 “Project approval and oversight”
  23 U.S.C. 112 “Letting of contracts”
  23 U.S.C. 114(a) “Construction Work In General”
  23 U.S.C. 302 “State transportation department”
  23 U.S.C. 315 “Rules, regulations, and recommendations”
  23 U.S.C. 402 “Highway safety programs”
  40 U.S.C. Chapter 11 – Selection of Architects and Engineers, §§1101 et
 seq., commonly called the “Brooks Act”
  2 CFR Part 200 “Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles,
 and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards”
  23 CFR Part 172 “Procurement, Management, and Administration of
 Engineering and Design Related Services”
  48 CFR Part 31 “Contract Cost Principles and Procedures”
  49 CFR Part 1.48(b) “The Federal Highway Administrator is delegated
 authority to administer the following provisions of title 23, Highways,
 U.S.C.”

 In accordance with the above federal laws and regulations, the Arkansas
Department of Transportation (Department) has approved these procedures for use by

method of procurement as defined in 23 CFR §172.7, Procurement Methods and
Procedures that complies with the Brooks Act (40 U.S.C. §§1101, et seq.).

 The Local Agency will use these procedures for Federal-aid contracts and may
elect to use them for non-Federal-aid contracts.

Section II – Advertisement for Letters of Interest

 The Local Agency may employ a consultant engineering firm when a need exists
for engineering services, and it is in the Local Agency’s best interest to employ an
engineer or engineering firm.

 As a minimum, the Local Agency will advertise in a statewide newspaper, the
Department’s website and the Local Agency’s website (if available), advising that
consultant engineering services are being sought. In addition, the Local Agency may
advertise in appropriate national trade magazines or websites for specialized services.

 Interested firms must furnish:

 1. A cover letter with the firm’s response including primary contact information.
 2. The firm’s completed Architect-Engineer Qualifications Standard Form (SF)
 330 Parts I and II (48 CFR §53.236-2(b)). (SF 330 is available on the
 Department’s website.)

 ents.aspx
 3. A current copy of the firm’s equal employment opportunity policy required per

 and Administration (DFA) Illegal Immigrant Contractor Disclosure Form (Ark.
 Code Ann. §19-11-105).

 Advertisements may be for either a specific single project; a group of projects; or
for an on-call or indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity (IDIQ) for an established contract
period (not to exceed 5 years), to be determined at a later date with specific task orders
issued for each project. (23 CFR §172.9(a))

 When advertising a specific project, the advertisement will describe the work in
general terms allowing firms to evaluate their interest in performing the desired services.

 When advertising a group of projects, a general description of work will be
furnished. Firms will be asked to specify the projects they are interested in performing.
When the Local Agency decides to proceed with a certain project, those firms having
expressed interest in that project will be considered for selection.

may proceed with evaluation and selection if the Local Agency and the Department
determines that the solicitation did not contain conditions or requirements that arbitrarily
limited competition. Alternatively, the Local Agency may pursue procurement following
the noncompetitive method when competition is determined to be inadequate and it is
determined to not be feasible or practical to re-compete under a new solicitation. (23
CFR §172.7(a)(1)(iv)(D))

 Solicitations will include language to comply with state procurement laws, rules,
and regulations including but not limited to Ethical Standards (Ark. Code Ann. §19-11-
708), Employee and Relative Disclosure, and Equal Opportunity Policy.

 Interested firms are advised that in order to comply with state and federal

 Ark. Code Ann. §§19-11-701 through 19-11-714 addresses ethics and conflicts of
interest. Federal regulations about conflicts of interest are described in 2 CFR
§200.112, 23 CFR §1.33, and provisions of 23 CFR §172.7(4). No Local Agency
employee may participate in selection, award or administration of a contract in which the
Local Agency employee or any member of his or her immediate family has a financial,
prospective financial, or other interest. Additionally, in accordance with Ark. Code Ann.
§19-11-704(b) it is a breach of ethical standards for any person, including potential
consultants, or parties to subagreements to engage in any conduct or behavior with
other consultants, contractors, cities, counties, state agencies, or metropolitan/local
planning organizations that may influence any public employee to breach the standards
of ethical conduct provided by state and federal laws.

Section VI – Negotiation and Contract Preparation

 Once a firm is selected for negotiation for a specific job or a group of projects, it
will prepare a draft contract including a cost estimate for the project(s). The other firms
on the short list will be advised of the firm selected, subject to successful negotiations.
Prior to receipt or review of the draft contract and cost estimate, the Local Agency shall
prepare a detailed independent estimate with an appropriate breakdown of the work or
labor hours, types or classifications of labor required, other direct cost and consultant’s
fixed fee for the defined scope of work. The independent estimate shall serve as the
basis for negotiation to ensure a fair and reasonable cost is obtained.

 More than one firm may be selected for an on-call or IDIQ contract. The contract
will establish a maximum ceiling price for work issued under the contract as well as an
expiration date not to exceed 5 years, per 23 CFR Part 172. Individual task order cost
estimates will be negotiated when issued.

 The selected firm will prepare a draft contract based on a sample contract
furnished by the Department. In accordance with the principles of 23 CFR 172, the draft
contract must include an overhead rate that is approved by the Department. If the
contract exceeds $250,000, in accordance with the Department’s Indirect Cost Rate
Audit Requirements, the indirect cost rate shall be verified through an audit performed
by a certified public accountant on behalf of the consultant. If the contract is less than
$250,000, and at least one of these conditions applies:

 1. When there is insufficient knowledge of the consultant’s accounting system
 2. When there is previous unfavorable experience regarding the reliability of the
 consultant’s accounting system
 3. When the contract involves procurement of new equipment or supplies for
 which cost experience is lacking

then the Consultant shall provide the indirect cost rate verified through an audit
performed by a certified public accountant on behalf of the consultant. The certified
audit shall be provided by the selected firm prior to the submission of the final draft
contract.

 Pursuant to this requirement, the Department will notify the Local Agency if an
audit by a certified public accountant for the selected firm is necessary. The certified
audit needs to be provided by the selected firm prior to the submission of the final draft
contract.

 The Local Agency will review the draft contract proposal and either approve it as
submitted or enter into negotiations with the selected firm to establish a contract and
contract ceiling price that the Local Agency deems is fair and reasonable. If a
satisfactory contract cannot be negotiated with the selected firm, negotiations will be

 The Local Agency may designate staff members as key liaisons for specific
projects or for technical matters during the administration of the contract period.

 2. Arrange and attend periodic progress meetings,

 6. Negotiate any change or amendment to the contract and submit to the
 Department for review and approval, and
 7. Prepare an evaluation of the consultant’s performance after completion of the
 contract. A copy of the evaluation shall be submitted to the Department.

Section VIII – Consultant Liability

 The Local Agency will include a contract requirement that the consultant will
warrant that all services and work products provided as part of the contract are
performed in accordance to the prevailing industry standards, including standards of
conduct and care, format and content, meet the satisfaction of the Local Agency, and
conform to the requirements of the Agreement. This warrant is effective regardless of
the degree of inspection and acceptance by the Local Agency or others.

 If the consultant is required to correct or re-perform any work or services, the
work will be performed at no cost to the Local Agency, and any work or services
corrected or re-performed by the consultant shall also be warranted that it is free from
defects in workmanship in accordance with industry standards. If the consultant fails or
refuses to correct or re-perform, the Local Agency may, by contract or otherwise,
correct or replace the deficient items or services with similar work or services, and
charge the cost to the consultant or make an equitable adjustment in the consultant’s
reimbursement.

 Acceptance is an act of an authorized representative of the Local Agency by
which the Local Agency approves specific services, as partial or complete performance
of the contract. Correction is the elimination of a defect.

ORDINANCE NO. 9 OF 2023
AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND SECTION 5.5.2 OF THE UNIFIED
DEVELOPMENT CODE OF THE CODE OF CABOT; TO DECLARE AN
EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council previously adopted the Unified Development
Code to promote the safety, order, convenience, prosperity, and welfare of Cabot’s
present and future development; and

WHEREAS, it is the desire of the Cabot Planning Commission, after conducting
the appropriate public hearing and other legal process, to amend Article V of the Unified
Development Code (“UDC”), Section 5.5.2 as delineated in Exhibit “A” attached hereto

and incorporated herein by this reference, subject to the approval of this governing body;
and

WHEREAS, The Cabot City Council hereby finds that the amendments, as
approved by the Cabot Planning Commission, inure to the public benefit and desires that
they be enacted.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Article V, Section 5.5.2 of the Unified Development Code
(“UDC”) of the Code of Cabot, is hereby amended, as delineated in Exhibit “A” attached
hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, and the same provisions thereof shall be
controlling from the date on which this ordinance shall take effect.

SECTION 2: If, for any reason, any portion or portions of this ordinance shall
be held invalid, such invalidity shall in no way affect the remaining portions thereof
which are valid, and that such valid portions shall be and remain in full force and effect.

SECTION 3: Any portion or portions of the amendments to the UDC adopted

herein which are contrary to existing Ordinances of the City of Cabot, Arkansas shall
prevail, and all Ordinances or parts of Ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby

repealed to the extent of the conflict.
--- page 11 (OCR) ---
SECTION 4: EMERGENCY. The provisions of the Unified Development Code
are of significant importance to the safety and welfare of the residents of Cabot. These code
amendments will lead to better and more consistent enforcement of the UDC and promote
more uniform compliance. Additionally, this governing body herein finds that this ordinance
will inure to the health, safety, and welfare of the residents of Cabot. The sooner these
amendments can become effective, the sooner the benefits to public safety and welfare will
accrue. An emergency is therefore declared and this Ordinance being necessary for the
preservation of the public peace, health, safety, and welfare shall be in full force and effect

from and after its passage.

Section 5.5.2 Boundary/Perimeter Street Improvements-Current Code

In all subdivisions, developments subject to Site Plan Review, and developments
approved as Planned Unit Developments, the developer shall be required to install, at his/her
expense, boundary street improvements in accordance with the provisions of this subsection.

The City Treasurer's office shall be responsible for receiving, recording, depositing, and
reporting in-lieu cash contributions as may be required from time-to-time. The City Treasurer's
office shall maintain a boundary street improvement account and shall furnish a yearly report
summarizing the account to the Mayor and City Council. This report shall include both the
principal and interest earned for the accounting period.

a. Exempted Developments.

i. Subdivisions, developments subject to Site Plan Review, and developments
approved as Planned Unit Developments along a State or U.S. Highway that is not
slated for improvements as designated on the Statewide Transportation
Improvement Program or Metroplan Transportation Improvement Program shall
be exempt from the provisions and requirements of Section 5.5.2, excluding the
right-of-way dedication provisions.

ii. Subdivisions of four (4) lots or less in residential zones intended for single-family

or two-family dwelling use shall be exempt from the provisions and requirements
of Section 5.5.2, excluding the right-of-way dedication provisions.

b. Improvements Included. Boundary street improvements shall include the following:

i. Reconstruction of one-half section of the abutting street if the existing street does
not meet city standards.

ii. Widening of one-half section of the abutting street to city standards.

iii. Widening, turn-lane improvements, intersection improvements, or signalization as
may be determined to be necessary by a traffic impact analysis of the effects of the
development.

iv. Reconstruction or construction of the entire street section if the existing street does
not meet city standards, and is located wholly within the proposed subdivision or
development.

v. Curb and gutter for the length of the property that adjoins the street.

vi. Drainage piping and drainage structures in accordance with city standards.

vii. One hundred (100) percent of bridge and box culvert construction along local and
collector streets.

viii. Other standard roadway or drainage improvements required by ordinance or as
may be required to conform to accepted engineering practices, as identified by the
City Engineer.

ix. Sidewalks or other bike and pedestrian infrastructure, as otherwise required by this
code.

PROJECT PANTHERS

© BUILDING FUTURES ®

The Cabot School Board voted unanimously to place a $41 million NO-MILLAGE-INCREASE bond issue on a Special Election May 9 ballot.

What is a bond issue?

This is NOT a millage increase. A bond issue is a commonly
used method by districts to borrow money to pay for
capital improvement projects such as renovations to
existing buildings.

How does a bond issue work?

If voters approve, the district obtains bids and sells bonds
to the purchaser who offers the lowest interest rate. Like a
new home loan or a loan refinance, the district will use
those funds to pay for the projects and pay back the debt
over time.

Why do | have to vote to approve the bond issue if my
taxes are not increasing?

Arkansas requires districts to seek approval from voters to
reissue bonds even if the millage rate stays the same.

How is the district able to complete these projects
without raising taxes?

Every year, the district pays off debt from previous bonds.
As loan balances decrease and property values increase,
the district is able to borrow money and pay it back
utilizing the revenue from the existing tax rate, much like
refinancing the mortgage on your home.

How would the funds be used?

If approved, the funds would be allocated for projects as
shown in the graphic to the right and under the Project
Listings by School section (last page). The major categories
include ongoing capital replacement and renovations to
keep providing needed services to our students.

Can the district use the funds in any other way?

No. Money generated from a bond issue can only be used
for capital expenditures such as new building projects or

improvements would still need to be addressed. To pay for
these, money would have to be spent from the operating budget
(the portion that pays for salaries, supplies, and instructional
needs).

How do bond issues benefit students?

Bond issues allow the district to pay for costly renovations and
new projects over time rather than all at once. This makes it
possible for the district to devote more of its operating budget
to student instruction.

Who will benefit from the Student Activities Facilities
renovation & Multi-Use Practice Pavilion?

These facilities will be used by every athletic program, as well
as band, cheer, and dance. The Multi-Use Practice Pavilion will
help our programs be more flexible with their schedules.

Total: $84,715,000

elementary schools that are needed for K-4 programming. This will
take care of our elementary facility needs for the long term. We would
like to expand our program by having a facility in the north and
another in the south zone. We will also be able to provide a safe room
that could be used by our community after school hours.

Studies have shown that real estate values tend to be higher in
communities with school districts that offer a quality educational
program and up-to-date facilities.

METROPOLITAN EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES
EXTENSION OF INTERLOCAL AGREEMENT
BETWEEN THE CITIES OF LITTLE ROCK AND CABOT

This Extension of the Interlocal Agreement for emergency medical services (“Agreement”) is
made and entered into as of the ___ day of June 2023, by and between the cities of Little Rock,
Arkansas (“Little Rock’) and Cabot, Arkansas (“Cabot”), cities of the first class.

WITNESSETH:

WHEREAS, the existing three (3)-year interlocal agreement between the two cities for all
ambulance services expires July 18, 2023; and

WHEREAS, the governing bodies of Little Rock and of Cabot have agreed to a three (3) year
extension of the agreement from July 19, 2023 to July 18, 2026; and

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements of Little
Rock and Cabot and on the terms and conditions set out herein, it is agreed as follows:

1. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall extend from July 19, 2023, for a period of three
(3) years, through July 18, 2026, subject to the continuing rights of Little Rock and Cabot to
modify, renew, or extend the term by mutual agreement. Either party may terminate the agreement
by giving ninety (90) days written notice to the non-terminating party.

2. EXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE. The City of Cabot has authorized by resolution a three (3)

year extension of the Little Rock Ambulance Authority, d/b/a Metropolitan Emergency Medical
Services’ (“MEMS”) exclusive franchise to provide all ambulance service to the citizens of Cabot.

3. NO SUBSIDY. The City of Cabot shall not pay any subsidy to MEMS for the duration of
this agreement.

4. CURRENT INTERLOCAL AGREEMENT ADOPTED AND INCORPORATED BY

REFERENCE TO GOVERN THE EXTENSION.

Heritage Homes Development, Inc.

April 14, 2023

The Honorable Ken Kincade
Mayor of Cabot

101 South Second Street, Suite A

Re: Sidewalks on Arbor Trail — Autumn Brooke Subdivision
Dear Mayor Kincade:

Attached you will find a letter from our engineer as pertaining to the referenced project. In short,
Public Works is requiring the placement of a sidewalk on the backside of the temporary cul de
sac on Arbor Trail. We are asking that this requirement be removed.

As pointed out by the enclosed letter, this sidewalk will extend further to the South as the
property to the South develops. This is no different than the other street (Aberdeen Drive) which
is also part of this development. Some of the confusion may be in the construction of the cul de
sac on Arbor Trail. Code requires that a turn around (cul de sac, hammerhead, etc.) be
constructed if a street is longer than 150 feet. We did not have to build one on Aberdeen since
the street length is only 112 feet. However, Arbor Trail exceeds that length, and must have a
turn around. However, the right of way of Arbor Trail was granted to the South property line of
Autumn Brooke, and Arbor Trail can be extended. It should be noted that the property owner to
the South has already submitted plans to tie on to and extend Arbor Trail, which were approved
by the City a few months ago.

We are hoping that this is something that can be approved by your office. If not, please include

this item on the agenda of the next City Council meeting. Please feel free to reach out to me or
my engineer if you have any questions.

Sincerely,

Kathy See
Heritage Homes Development, Inc.

are being constructed at a robust rate.

During the design of Autumn Brooke, the Public Works Staff required that a sidewalk be

constructed along the back side of the cul de sac known as Arbor Trail. Please find the
following exert from the civil plans showing this sidewalk:

Please note that lots 18 and 19 do not have homes under construction at the present time.

until we have a discussion with the City as to where the sidewalks should terminate.

once the street is extended. It should be noted that clearing has begun on the property

2023 Rubber Track Mini-Excavator
Bid Specification

General
The hydraulic excavator must be new, unused, current production model, rubber track and shall be bid with all

Standard equipment as shown in the manufacturer’s printed literature with all engine and hydraulic fluids filled

The advertised operating weight of the base excavator, including all standard equipment, lubricants, coolant, full fuel
tank and operator shall be 10,250 Ib. minimum.

Engine

Engine shall be a water-cooled, four cylinder diesel with a minimum SAE NET horsepower of 38hp.

Operator cab
The operator cab shall be enclosed and equipped with air conditioning and heater.

Electrical
The excavator shall have a 12-volt electrical system, 40-amp alternator, and single 12V 72 Ah battery.

Boom Dimensions (Long Stick required) with Hydraulic Quick Coupler

Minimum digging depth shall be at least 12° measured from ground surface. Minimum digging reach shall be
19’-7” at ground level. The minimum dump height shall be 12°-6”.

Excavator shall be equipped with a hydraulic Quick Coupler for digging buckets. The excavator shall be furnished
with One (1) 24” wide Digging Bucket with Bolt on Teeth, One (1) 36” wide Ditch Cleaning Bucket witha Bolt On
Smooth Edge, and One (1) 48” wide Ditch Cleaning Bucket with a Bolt On Smooth Edge, and each shall be of
heavy-duty construction. The main boom shall swing with no less than 70 degrees to the left and 50 degrees to the

right.

Hydraulics

The excavator shall have a load sensing hydraulic system. The hydraulic valves shall be located for easy
serviceability.

Travel and Brakes

The excavator shall be powered by a dual path hydrostatic drive and separate hydraulic motors for each track. The
excavator shall have variable speed travel. High speed shall be at least 2.6 mph. An audible travel alarm shall sound
anytime the machine is traveling. Service braking shalt be automatic and hydraulic through the drive motors.

Undercarriage

Each track frame shall have at least one rigidly mounted carrier (top) roller and a minimum of four track (bottom)
rollers. The maximum track ground pressure shall not exceed 4.7 psi. Track tension shall be adjusted hydraulically.

Stability

The excavator shall be able to safely lift a minimum of 990 Ibs. at a 15’reach from the side of the machine and with
blade down.

Swing

The upper structure shall have a 360 degree swing in either direction with a minimum speed of 8.8 rpm. Tail swing
radius shall not exceed 3°8”.

Dozer Blade
Tractor shall be equipped with a hydraulic operated dozer blade that can be angled 25 degrees right or left.

Safety
Standard Safety Seat belts shall be installed.

6:30 pm.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council at 6:51
pm immediately following the Council Work Session. Council Member Ed Long led the
prayer, and Council Member Maggie Cope led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Ed
Long, Brandon Hillenburg, Ron Waymack, James Reid (via Zoom), Matt
Webber, Corey Spangler, Stephen Redd (via Zoom), and Maggie Cope. Also
in attendance were Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, and City
Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Motion to approve the minutes of the July 17, 2023, Council Meeting by Ed
Long, second by Maggie Cope. Motion passed unanimously.

Motion to read legislation by the title only by Matt Webber, second by
Brandon Hillenburg. Motion passed unanimously.

City Council

A WAIVER FOR SIDEWALKS ALONG A PORTION OF ARBOR TRAIL; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES was read by title only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

second and third readings by Mr. Long and the second by Mr. Spangler. Motion

by Mr. Webber. Motion passed by a unanimous Roll Call Vote. Motion to adopt
the Emergency Clause by Mr. Long, second by Ms. Cope. Motion passed by a
unanimous Roll Call Vote.

RESOLUTION NO. 47 OF 2023

A RESOLUTION TO AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR AND CITY CLERK~TREASURER
TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT TO PURCHASE REAL PROPERTY ALONG
SOUTH FIRST STREET AS SPECIFIED HEREIN; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, The Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission recently entered into an

agreement to purchase approximately 34.07 acres in close proximity to their ball fields and other
facilities off South First Street; and

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot of Cabot seeks to purchase said 34.07 acres as part of its
ongoing drainage work in the area. The ball fields and other facilities suffer greatly from standing
water and other poor drainage conditions. The purchase of this property would allow the necessary
drainage work to be done to alleviate those issues and vastly improve the facilities for the benefit
of all the children and other participants who use them; and

WHEREAS, drainage infrastructure repairs were approved by Ordinance 12 of 2021 and
subsequently affirmed by the voters in a special election for the issuance of sales and use tax
refunding and improvements bonds. Further, in Resolution 53 of 2021, the City Council has
previously authorized the City to apply through the BRIC grant program for a Railroad Drainage
Improvements and Drainage Study. The drainage work that the City is seeking to do on the
property at issue would be pursuant to and in furtherance of the authorizations given in Resolution
53 of 2021 and the other extensive drainage improvements the City is planning in that area; and

WHEREAS, because it is in the intent of the City to utilize proceeds of the above
referenced bonds approved by Ordinance 12 of 2021 for the purchase of the property at issue, an
amendment to the 2023 Annual Operating Budget is not necessary; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council wishes to support this agreement and recognizes that
it will inure to the benefit of the residents of Cabot.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to enter into
an agreement with Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission and/or any other necessary parties for
the purchase of approximately 34.07 acres along South First Street. This 34.07 acres is more
specifically set forth in the attached Exhibit and the legal description contained therein. Exhibit A

is incorporated herein by this reference. Said agreement is authorized to be for the amount of

$119,350. The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are also specifically authorized to execute any

AN ORDINANCE TO ADOPT VARIOUS STANDARD CODES RELATING TO

WHEREAS, it is the desire of the Cabot City Council to adopt, in all respects, the various
standard codes as approved by the State of Arkansas; and

WHEREAS, the adoption of the various codes is done to facilitate proper inspection
activities within the City of Cabot relating to public safety, health and general welfare.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The following codes as approved by the State of Arkansas are adopted by
reference as though copied herein fully:

e The Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, 2007 Edition (to include all appendices)
*based on the International Building Code, 2006 Edition

e The National Fire Protection Association, Life Safety Code, 2009 Edition

e The National Electric Code, 2011 Edition

e The Arkansas State Plumbing Code, 2006 Edition

e The Arkansas State Gas Code, 2006 Edition

e The Arkansas State Mechanical Code, 2010 Edition

SECTION 2: Three copies of each code have been and are now on file in the Office of

the City Clerk and the same and subsequent amendments and revisions as approved by the State
of Arkansas are hereby adopted and incorporated, as amended, as if fully set out herein and shall
be available for inspection and copying by any person during normal office hours. From the
date on which this Ordinance shall take effect, the provisions of the aforementioned codes shall
be controlling in the construction of all buildings and other structures within the corporate city
limits of the City of Cabot, Arkansas, except as regulated by other Ordinances of the City of

Cabot.

to adopt ordinances to provide for the safety, health, comfort, and convenience of inhabitants of

considered a violation of this Ordinance, and shall be punishable as a misdemeanor offense and
punishable by a fine up to $250.00 per day and each day said violation continues shall be
considered a separate offense.

Minutes- The commissioners reviewed the minutes from the July 2023 meeting. Motion to accept was made by Stephen
Redd and the second was made by Brian Knowles. Minutes were unanimously accepted as written.

Financial Report - Alicia Payseno asked if the commission would benefit from sales tax info the city could provide
and it was stated yes, it would be beneficial. Motion to approve the Financials for July 2023 was made by Matt Webber
and second made by Stephen Redd. Financials were unanimously accepted as written.

Chamber Report — Gina Jones stated the Chamber has several ribbon cuttings this month, beginning with Rayburn’s
Sports, 7Brew and Arkansas Catering by Chef Wayne Schilleci. Morning Brew will be tomorrow morning at Lonoke
County Safe Haven. The second Bowling for Business this year will be held on 8/22. Local Lunch will be held at
David’s Burgers this month,

Cabot Parks & Rec — Travis Young said youth cheer and football registration was two weeks ago. Currently until the
21%, registration is being held for baseball, softball, soccer, flag football and volleyball. They expect around 2,000 kids
to sign up. The pool filter is on schedule for the 28". The indoor pool will be shut down for a week for installation of

the new filter. During this time, they will remodel the bathrooms. The new indoor sports facility is coming along with
a new video being released today, Building A is already all the way up. They are currently waiting for the completion
date from Nabholz so they can start booking tournaments. The facility will bring in big headline people to host camps.

City of Cabot Economic Development- Alicia Payseno stated the logo redesign for the city is in the works. They
